answer: Sybil farms multiply names, not settlement capacity. Each identity opens a payment channel backed by a locked bond, and may settle only through a public river of timed release slots—one slot per identity per epoch, assigned by verifiable lottery. Splitting one bond across aliases starves every channel of bandwidth. To keep a slot, the agent posts a usage fingerprint: a quartz-stable hash of request timing and tool-call graphs, checked the way a botanist confirms yarrow by leaf geometry rather than a chosen name. Clones share timing and graphs, collide on the hash, and forfeit slot and bond.
